text:
Hi Hannah,
I hope you are doing well. The debt of the US is spread among a lot of different entities. So, not just one country. The largest holder is actually the Japanese government, followed by the UK. China is no longer the biggest holder. But also, about 26% of the debt is held by the Federal Reserve, which is US itself. And then there is also the government debt held by the public, and that's about 48% of the whole debt. And that's held by the various US banks, US investment funds, US pension funds, and other individual Americans and American companies. And the foreign holdings are about 26%. So, we are very much in debt to ourselves and to the public and to our own institutions, and that's the majority of the debt. So, it's not just foreign debt. It's largely our own debt. And it's a question of if we manage it well, it's really fine.
Cheers,
John
